verdict: Right winner, right size. Slow game kept the total under.

factors.text: Slow game: 96 and 93 possessions against a slate average of 102. Fewer possessions, fewer points on both sides.
Washington made 8 of 32 threes (25%) while taking 32, and Cleveland won the offensive rebounds 15 to 5 (19 second-chance points to 8).
Harden scraped his PRA line (24 against 23.5) despite 5 of 18 shooting, thanks to 6 assists and 4 of 4 free throws. Mobley and Allen cleared; Young and Davis are not in the box-score feed.

verdict: Wrong winner and wrong total. The biggest pick miss of the day.

factors.text: Both teams took 96 shots (slate average 87) at 107 and 108 possessions (slate 102). Fast game, so the under lean was fighting the pace.
Atlanta allowed 129 against its usual 111.8. Miami scored 70 points in the paint (35 of 56, 62.5%), made 27 of 44 at the rim, ran 21 fast-break points and grabbed 12 offensive rebounds.
Miami shot 23 free throws to Atlanta's 14, and Atlanta committed 24 fouls to Miami's 17.
Our stats model backed Atlanta by 13 because Miami started 0-4, but the market had it at 2.5. Four-game samples exaggerate a bad start, and the market was closer to right.

verdict: Right winner and the under hit.

factors.text: Indiana made 9 of 36 threes (25%) and Nembhard and Nesmith went a combined 10 of 32 from the field. Indiana was missing Zubac, McConnell and Sheppard, as we flagged.
Indiana shot 35 free throws (28 made) and still scored only 109, so the under needed the cold three-point shooting.
Philadelphia scored 39 in the fourth against Indiana's 21 after being outscored 36-13 in the third. Close games like this can flip, so the pick was right but not safe.
Maxey (36 PRA), Embiid (34 PRA), Siakam, LeBron and Walker all cleared their lines.

verdict: Winner and margin nailed (8.4 projected, 8 actual). Total 29 under.

factors.text: Charlotte turned it over 25 times (13 Detroit steals) and had only 71 shots. Combined shots were 147 against a slate average of 174.
Detroit's defence rated about 90 per 100 possessions and held Charlotte to 89 against its usual 104. Detroit scored 97 against a usual 113, so both sides were below normal.
95 possessions, among the slowest games of the day (Cleveland-Washington was 96 and 93).
Charlotte was without Knueppel, White and G. Williams, which we allowed for. It still undersold how thin that offence was: 17 assists to 25 turnovers.

verdict: Right winner by 23 more than projected. The under missed.

factors.text: Orlando gave it away 20 times (Wagner 7) and Toronto turned that into 20 points off turnovers, 23 fast-break points and 15 steals.
Toronto shot 42.9% from three and made 26 of 31 free throws; Orlando shot 28.6% from three and Bane went 3 of 14.
Orlando was without Banchero, Suggs and Isaac. We knew, but a thin roster plus turnovers compounds: the margin ended at 30, with Toronto up by as many as 33.
With a 30-point gap, the total was inflated by bench minutes (Orlando's bench scored 50), and the Wagner points leg missed (15 against 17.5) in a game his team trailed from the first quarter.

verdict: Right winner and the over hit, but the margin was 25 bigger than projected.

factors.text: Houston shot 64.9% effective (46 of 84, 17 of 38 threes, 79% at the rim). Milwaukee shot 40.2% and 29.3% from three on 41 attempts.
Houston blocked 10 shots to Milwaukee's 3 and took 12 steals. Milwaukee allowed 132 against a usual 122.2, and was held to 100 against a usual 116.8.
Houston was without Sengun and Adams and still won by 32, so depth (VanVleet 24, Bogdanovic 16 on 5 of 6, Durant 18) was undervalued.
Jaquez (25 PRA against 30.5) and Turner (2 rebounds against 4.5) missed on stretch legs; Smith's threes cleared.

verdict: Right winner and margin. The under missed by 25.5, the biggest wrong total.

factors.text: New York took 105 shots (slate average 87) because it grabbed 16 offensive rebounds, giving it 21 second-chance attempts and 23 second-chance points.
Both teams hit threes at a high rate on high volume: New York 22 of 48 (45.8%), Chicago 18 of 42 (42.9%), against a slate rate of 35.8%. Together they took 90 threes (slate average 73).

Chicago came in allowing 129.5 a game, the most of any team that played today, and New York scored 133. Our stats model leaned on New York's slow 104-a-game style (model total 224.8) and underrated how much Chicago gives up.
The two teams scored 74 in the fourth quarter alone (New York 43).

verdict: Wrong winner by a possession or two. Free throws and second chances decided it.

factors.text: Golden State shot 37 free throws (30 made) to Minnesota's 27 (19 made). Curry scored 44 on 27 shots with 16 of 16 from the line.
Golden State grabbed 13 offensive rebounds to Minnesota's 8 and scored 22 points off turnovers to Minnesota's 13.
Minnesota made 15 of 45 threes (33%); LaMelo shot 3 of 11 with 6 turnovers and Gobert went 0 for 4 with 1 point, which sank his PRA leg (6 against 20.5).
Minnesota allowed 119 against a usual 105, so its best trait did not show up. Minnesota was also without Edwards, which we had already priced in.
Our stats model had Minnesota by 9.3 against the market's 3.5, driven by its 3-1 home record. As with Atlanta, we leaned toward the stats model where it disagreed with the market and lost.

verdict: Right winner (Low confidence combined). Total 45.5 under, the biggest total miss.

factors.text: New Orleans made 7 of 30 threes (23.3%) and shot 41.5% overall, scoring 91 against a usual 124.7.
New Orleans turned it over 19 times to Denver's 18 (Denver took 11 steals), and Denver led 37-18 after the first quarter.
Denver's defence rated about 87.5 per 100 possessions and held New Orleans to a 87.8 offensive rating. Denver also shot 94.7% from the line.

These teams met earlier this season in a 141-135 game (276 points). With three or four games each, that one result and both teams' early scoring averages pushed our projected total to 240.9, nearly 46 points too high.
The box-score feed lists only part of each roster. Jokic is not in Denver's list, so we cannot confirm his minutes or whether he played, and his rebounds leg could not be graded.

verdict: Right winner (High confidence), but the Spurs won by 6 where we projected 9.9 and the market had 11.5. Total 228 against 233.5, no lean.

factors.text: Spurs scored 54 points in the paint to the Jazz 34, took 101 shots to 92 and won the offensive rebounds 15 to 12.
Jazz turned it over 19 times to the Spurs 11, which gave San Antonio 17 points off turnovers.
Utah made 15 of 39 threes (38.5%) and George scored 31 with 5 threes, which kept the Jazz closer than the 11.5-point spread. The Jazz bench outscored the Spurs bench 39 to 19.
Wembanyama had 36 points, 14 rebounds and 5 assists on 14 of 25 shooting, clearing his PRA line of 27.5 by a wide margin.
Our margin was 3.9 off, the posted spread 5.5 off, so the model beat the market here.

verdict: Wrong winner (Medium confidence): Dallas won 120-96, a 24-point swing from our pick. The under lean hit, 216 against 228.5.

factors.text: OKC made 5 of 32 (15.6%) while Dallas made 16 of 45 (35.6%): that is a 33-point gap from threes alone, far outside what either team's early numbers suggest. Mostly shooting variance.
Dallas had 17 fast-break points to OKC 0. The Thunder trailed only 65-59 at halftime, then were outscored 55-37 in the second half.
Gilgeous-Alexander shot 7 of 19 (1 of 6 from three) for 21 points; Flagg had 26 points and 8 assists for Dallas.
Dallas won second-chance points 18 to 7 and the offensive rebound count 15 to 12.
OKC were missing J. Williams, Holmgren, Wallace and Caruso, so depth was thin; our model was already close to the market (6.0 against 5.5) and both missed by about 30.

verdict: Right winner (Medium confidence), Lakers by 16 against our 4.2 and the market's 5.5. The over lean missed badly: 190 against 228.5.

factors.text: Lakers shot 44.3% (35 of 79) and the Clippers 35.1% (26 of 74), both teams went 9 and 10 of 31 from three. The Clippers scored 87 against a usual 113.0 and the Lakers 103 against a usual 128.2.

About 98 possessions a team (feed has no possession count, estimated from shots, free throws, turnovers and offensive rebounds) against a slate average of 102, so the over lean was fighting a slower game.
Lakers outscored the Clippers 48 to 28 in the paint and 24 to 6 on the fast break; the Clippers turned it over 24 times and Lakers scored about 31 points off them.

Clippers were missing Ingram, Beal, Hachimura and Strus; Wagler (21 on 4 of 15) and Garland (14 on 4 of 12) carried a thin offence. Our over lean used 4-game scoring averages (Lakers 128.2) that did not hold up.
The Lakers led 94-76 with 6:25 left and scored only 9 more points, which suggests late bench minutes cut the total, but the feed has no minutes by quarter so this is an inference.

headline: Winners 9 of 12, but margins and totals were no better than the market

stats.label: Winners
stats.note: All 5 High-confidence picks won; Medium 4 of 7. Misses: Atlanta, Minnesota and Oklahoma City.

stats.label: Total leans
stats.note: Hit: Indiana-Philadelphia under, Houston-Milwaukee over, Oklahoma City-Dallas under. Missed: Atlanta, Toronto, New York, Lakers-Clippers (over lean, game finished 190 against 228.5).

stats.label: Total error
stats.note: Average miss of our projected total over 12 games. The posted totals missed by 16.2, so we matched the market (0.4 better) but did not beat it clearly.

stats.label: Margin error
stats.note: Average miss of our projected margin. The posted spreads missed by 10.7, so the market was about 1 point closer.

stats.label: Top props
stats.note: Brunson 46 (line 24.5), Maxey 36 (31.5), Embiid 34 (29.5), Mitchell 31 (29.5), Harden 24 (23.5), Wembanyama 36 pts + 14 reb + 5 ast (27.5), Reaves 16 points (14.5). Towns is not in the feed.

stats.label: Slip legs
stats.note: 62% of the 74 legs we could grade (points 9 of 18, rebounds 13 of 17, PRA 13 of 18, assists 6 of 12, threes 5 of 9). No slip cleared all four legs; 7 are still undecided because 22 legs are on players missing from the box-score feed.

right: All five High-confidence moneylines won (Cleveland, Detroit, Houston, New York, San Antonio), and Detroit's margin was almost exact (8.4 projected, 8 actual).
The seven single-stat top props that could be graded all cleared, mostly in PRA, where one weak scoring night is covered by rebounds and assists.
Toronto, Houston, Denver and the Lakers were right on the winner even when we expected a much closer game; San Antonio's margin was 3.9 off against 5.5 for the spread.
Rebounds and PRA legs held up on the slips: rebounds 13 of 17 and PRA 13 of 18.
wrong: The market's margin was closer than our stats model's in the games where the two disagreed most (Atlanta by 10.5 points, Denver 10.2, Cleveland 8.7, Minnesota 5.8). We leaned on the model for Atlanta and Minnesota and lost both; we leaned on the market for Denver and won. Four-game samples overstated Miami's bad start and Minnesota's home record.

Totals: 4 of our 7 total leans missed. The biggest total misses (Denver-New Orleans -45.5, Lakers-Clippers -38.5, Charlotte-Detroit -29.5, New York-Chicago +25.5) came from game-to-game swings in turnovers and three-point shooting rather than anything the 3-4 game samples could show. The Lakers-Clippers over lean ran into a slower game (about 98 possessions) with both teams shooting 29-32% from three or worse.

Oklahoma City was a Medium pick that lost by 24: the Thunder made 5 of 32 threes against 16 of 45 for Dallas. That is mostly variance, though thin OKC depth (four players out) also meant a few early misses could not be absorbed.
Slips: the 'safe' legs are meant to be floors that cleared every game this season, but only 62% of the gradable legs cleared. Points legs hit 9 of 18 and assists 6 of 12.

Blowouts (Toronto +30, Houston +32, Oklahoma City-Dallas 24, Denver +13) probably cut starters' minutes, which hurts floors on points and assists. The feed has no minutes by quarter, so this is an inference.
change: Cut the stats model's weight when it disagrees with the market by more than 5 points on the margin, until teams have 8+ games.
Show 'Coin toss' on totals until both teams have 6+ games, and weight the market total more heavily early in the season.
Flag slip legs on a team that is a 10+ point favourite or underdog as blowout risk.
Add minutes and turnover data to the box-score pull so garbage time and turnover-driven misses can be separated from shooting luck.
caveats: The box-score feed lists only part of each roster for some games, so 22 slip legs and the Towns top-prop leg could not be graded. 'Usual' scoring figures use each team's 3 to 4 games this season; the feed has no season shot averages, so shot volume is compared with the slate average (87 shots, 36.5 threes, 102 possessions a team). Lakers-Clippers: possessions are estimated and second-chance points were not provided.

verdict: Right winner on a Low-confidence near pick-em: Atlanta won 114-111, almost exactly our 2-point margin. Total finished 225 against 237.5, 12.5 under.

factors.text: About 99 possessions for each side against 102 on last slate's average, with both teams on the second night of a back-to-back. Fewer possessions kept the total 12.5 under the posted 237.5 (our projection was 237.0).

Atlanta made 17 of 43 threes (40%) to Cleveland's 13 of 42 (31%); Mitchell shot 7 of 19 with 1 of 9 from three. Atlanta also won the fast break 15 to 4 and the offensive rebounds 15 to 9, while Cleveland won the free-throw line (22 of 29 against 13 of 18). Nothing here separates the teams by more than a few possessions' luck: a coin-flip game decided by a 12-point three-point gap.

Okongwu scored 29 on 11 of 17 and Alexander-Walker 25; Wiggins added 20 off the bench (+17) in 24 minutes. McCollum was 1 of 8 for 5 points. Starters played 30 to 36 minutes in a 3-point game, so there was no garbage-time effect.

Totals were Coin toss under the 6-game safeguard, so no lean was graded. The market-weighted 237.5 missed by 12.5; our model-only total (235.4) would have missed by 10.4, so weighting the market did not help here.

verdict: Right winner at 66%, but New Orleans won by 12 against a projected 5.5. Total finished 252 against 237.5, 14.5 over; the Coin toss label kept us off an under.

factors.text: About 114 possessions for each team against a slate average of 102, with 63 fast-break points between them (34 New Orleans, 29 Sacramento). Sacramento turned it over 25 times and New Orleans took 18 steals, a turnover-driven open game that neither team's 4-game average (233 and 238 totals) showed.

New Orleans shot 50 of 84 (60%) and scored 80 in the paint (Williamson 10 of 12) against a Sacramento defence that already allowed 125.5 a game (29th). That is mostly an efficiency and turnover result, not three-point luck: both teams were near average from three (SAC 32%, NOP 34%).

We took 2 points off New Orleans for the back-to-back and 1 for Poole doubtful; the Pelicans won comfortably anyway. The market (NOP -5.5) missed by the same 6.5 points as our projection, so neither side had an edge. Sacramento starters played 37 to 41 minutes, so this was not a garbage-time result.

Total safeguard worked as intended: the 25% model / 75% market total of 237.5 was still 14.5 low, and the alternate "under 243.5" idea would also have missed. Both defences ranked 25th or worse, which a 4-game sample understated. Blowout-risk flag did not apply (spread 5.5).

verdict: Wrong winner and our biggest miss: Memphis won 124-103 as an underdog (+235) while we had Portland by 7. Total finished 227, 6.5 under 233.5.

factors.text: Memphis made 18 of 42 threes (43%) and all 12 free throws; Portland made 12 of 49 (24%), with Lillard 1 of 9, Holiday 2 of 5 and Avdija 0 of 4. Memphis also took 102 shots to Portland's 91 (15 offensive rebounds, 11 turnovers against Portland's 16). Mostly shooting variance, but Memphis was already 4-0 with the 4th-ranked defence (107.0 allowed).

Portland's 3-0 start (129.3 scored, 1st offence) was the whole case for the margin; Memphis was 4-0 as well, and the market only had Portland -7.5. The model and market margins (6.5 and 7.5) were both 28 points wide of the 21-point Memphis win, so the safeguard against model-market gaps (gap 1.0) correctly did not trigger and would not have helped.

Memphis led by up to 24, but minutes look normal (Boozer 28, Coward 27, Grant 27; Portland starters 23 to 32), so garbage time explains little. The score was settled by Memphis bench scoring: Stewart 18 in 16 minutes and Post 10 in 7.
Coin toss total (233.5 posted, 233.0 projected) finished 227, 6.5 low: Portland's offence scored 26 under its average. No total lean was graded.

headline: Winners 2 of 3: both favourites held, but Memphis ran over Portland

stats.label: Winners
stats.note: Atlanta (Low) and New Orleans (Medium) won; Portland (Medium) lost 124-103 to Memphis, the underdog at +235. Very small sample.

stats.label: Total leans
stats.note: All three totals were Coin toss under the 6-game safeguard, so none were graded. Totals finished 225, 252 and 227 against 237.5, 237.5 and 233.5 posted.

stats.label: Total error
stats.note: Average miss of our projected total over 3 games (12.0, 16.4, 6.0). The posted totals missed by 11.2, so the market was 0.3 closer; our model-only totals missed by 12.4.

stats.label: Margin error
stats.note: Average miss of our projected margin (1.0, 6.5, 28.0). The posted spreads missed by 12.2, so we were 0.3 closer; the model-only margins missed by 11.5. The Memphis result alone drives both.

stats.label: Top props
stats.note: No top-prop picks were on file for these three games when this review ran, so none are graded.

stats.label: Slip legs
stats.note: No slip legs were on file for these games when this review ran. Box scores with minutes are saved for later grading.

right: Atlanta (55%) and New Orleans (66%) were the right sides, and Atlanta's margin was within one point of our 2.0 projection.
The Coin toss totals avoided total leans in three games that finished 12.5 under, 14.5 over and 6.5 under the posted lines.
Margin weighting 55/45 kept our margin error 0.3 points better than the posted spreads over the three games, with no extra model-market gap needing a fix.
wrong: Memphis-Portland: we had Portland by 7 and the market had them by 7.5, but Memphis won by 21 on 18 of 42 threes against Portland's 12 of 49 and 15 offensive rebounds. Mostly shooting variance on top of a 3-0 start that was a small sample.

Kings-Pelicans: the total finished 252, 14.5 over the posted line and 16.4 above our projection. Both teams were winless with poor defences (29th and 25th) and the game was played at about 114 possessions with 63 fast-break points; four-game samples understated both.
The back-to-back and injury adjustments we made to New Orleans (about 3 points) pointed the wrong way: the Pelicans won by 12.
change: Keep the market-weighted totals until teams have 6+ games: model-only totals missed by 12.4 against 11.5 for our blended totals, but a mixed result over three games is not enough to change the weights.
Add a pace and turnover note to the totals page for winless or high-turnover teams: Sacramento's 25 turnovers fed 40 points off turnovers in the game.
Treat early 3-0 and 4-0 records the same on both sides: Memphis was 4-0 with a top-5 defence, so Portland's 3-0 home start should not have outweighed that in the margin.
caveats: Only three games, so every error figure is noisy. The feed has no second-chance or bench points; possessions are estimated (FGA + 0.44 FTA - ORB + TOV). No prop or slip picks for these games were on file, so those are not graded. Poole's status is not in the box score feed.

verdict: Right winner (the underdog flag paid off), wrong size: Washington won by 16 against our 0.3. Total 174 was 44.5 under the posted 218.5, the lowest of the day.

factors.text: Charlotte made 12 of 56 threes (21%) and 35.6% effective FG on 101 shots, with Miller 7 of 24 and Reid 5 of 17. Washington made 29 of 35 free throws (Davis 9 of 10, Young 12 of 14) against Charlotte's 7 of 12. Mostly shooting variance plus a free-throw gap of 23 attempts.
About 100 and 94 possessions against a slate average of 99.6, so pace did not cause the 174 total; the misses did. Charlotte's 18 offensive rebounds did not make up for 56 threes at 21%.

Charlotte played without Knueppel, White, G. Williams and Boswell and Schroder (questionable, foot) played 29 minutes with 6 fouls. The thin lineup is a plausible reason for the poor shot quality, but the sample cannot separate it from variance.

Margin safeguard (market-weighted, model +4.5 for WAS vs market -1.5) moved the pick to a 0.3-point lean; the model-only margin (11.5 off) would have been closer than the blend (15.7) or the market (17.5), so here the safeguard cost accuracy though the winner was right either way. Coin toss total correctly stayed ungraded: model-only 219.3 and market 218.5 both missed by about 45.

verdict: Right winner and almost exact: Boston won by 14 against our 14.3 and the 14.5 spread, and the 236 total was 0.5 over the posted 235.5.

factors.text: Boston made 42 of 82 (57.3% effective FG) and scored 58 in the paint against Chicago's 40, while Chicago took 20 offensive rebounds and 50 threes (15 made) and still fell short.
Despite a 14.5-point spread the Celtics starters played normal minutes (Tatum 35, Pritchard 35), so no garbage-time sitting. A blowout-risk flag on slip legs would not have hurt or helped here.
Pritchard scored 30 on 9 of 17 with 9 of 9 free throws and Chicago's Wilson hit 6 of 11 threes; the swings roughly cancelled in the margin.

verdict: Right winner, bigger margin: Detroit won by 16 against our 7.2 (market 8.5). Total 204 was 18.5 under the posted 222.5.

factors.text: Brooklyn turned it over 24 times (Randle 5, Traore 3, Clowney 3) against Detroit's 12; Detroit scored 27 fast-break points to Brooklyn's 11 and took 14 steals. That explains most of the extra margin.
Detroit made 12 of 41 threes and 38 of 90 overall (48.9% effective FG) and Brooklyn 31 of 77. Neither team shot well, so the total finished under; about 104 possessions each is normal pace.

Bench scoring was even (Detroit 46, Brooklyn 48) and both teams took similar shots, so the extra margin came from turnovers rather than talent; Holland scored 18 in 22 minutes and Wagner 16 for Brooklyn.

verdict: Wrong winner by a hair: Philadelphia won 98-93 against our pick-em lean on New York (0.0). Total 191 was 35.5 under the posted 226.5 in a 91-possession game.

factors.text: Both teams played about 91 possessions against a slate average of 99.6, the slowest game of the day, which on its own is worth well over 10 points of total.
Philadelphia had 57.3% effective FG on 37 of 75 and Maxey scored 27, while New York made 13 of 41 threes and Brunson shot 8 of 22 (24 points). New York took 14 offensive rebounds to 5 and still lost.

Margin safeguard (model PHI +3.6 vs market NYK -1.5) put us on a 0.0 pick-em; the model-only margin was 1.4 off and the blend 5.0, so the safeguard cost accuracy again. Coin toss total correctly stayed ungraded (model-only 218.8 was also 28 high).
Starters played normal minutes (Embiid 33, Maxey 38, Brunson 35); no foul trouble beyond Simons' 4 fouls in 31 minutes.

verdict: Wrong winner and a big miss: Orlando won 121-114 as a 5.5-point underdog while we had Toronto by 8.6 at 72%. Total 235 was 7.5 over the posted 227.5.

factors.text: Orlando made 18 of 34 threes (64.9% effective FG) with Bane 6 of 12 and 28 points, Cain 5 of 5 and da Silva 3 of 5; Toronto made 11 of 27. Orlando's shooting night is variance on a team that entered with a 1-3 record and the 119.5 allowed average.
Only about 91 and 94 possessions, so the total went over on efficiency (Orlando 121 points on 91 possessions), not tempo.

Orlando played without Banchero, Suggs, Isaac, Penda and Nelson yet used a 10-man rotation; Wagner, Carter and Bane each played 39. Toronto's Barnes scored 41 on 19 of 34, a volume night that did not carry the team.

The market-weighted margin (model TOR +15.8 vs market +5.5) was the right call: the model-only margin was 22.8 off, the blend 15.6 and the market 12.5. Without the safeguard the pick would have been even more confident. Free throws also swung it: Orlando shot 25 of 29 to Toronto's 11 of 15 and Toronto had 33 fouls.

verdict: Wrong winner, close game: Dallas won 116-111 against our Houston lean (5.2). Total 227 was only 3.5 over the posted 223.5.

factors.text: Houston played without Alperen Sengun and Reed Sheppard (both did not play, low back soreness); Sheppard was already out and Sengun was only questionable on the morning report. Durant played 37 minutes. Losing Sengun is a plausible reason the 5-0 team lost, but one game cannot prove it.
Houston made 7 of 29 threes (24%) against Dallas's 12 of 33, and Dallas had 28 fast-break points to Houston's 10 despite 18 turnovers. Flagg (33) and Irving (35) shot 25 of 38 between them.

Houston still took 96 shots to Dallas's 81 and 20 offensive rebounds to 12, so the loss is mostly three-point shooting variance plus the injuries, not a flaw in the margin; the market missed by 11.5 against our 10.2.
Houston's 5-0 start (123.0 scored, 108.8 allowed) was the case for the pick, and the 5-game sample plus a questionable Sengun was why confidence stayed at Medium.

verdict: Right winner, much bigger than expected: Miami won 145-125 against our 5.6 (market 8.5). Total 270 was 32.5 over the posted 237.5.

factors.text: Miami made 54 of 93 (67.7% effective FG) and 64 points in the paint, with Antetokounmpo 31 pts, 18 reb and 10 ast in 31 minutes, Adebayo 27 on 11 of 14 and Thompson 7 of 12 from three. Indiana also shot 57.7% effective FG on 44 of 91.

Indiana without Haliburton and Zubac (Zubac listed out, DNP coach's decision) used a 11-man rotation led by Nembhard 22 and Quenton Jackson 24 off the bench; the thin interior gave up the paint (64-50).
About 104 possessions each against a slate average of 99.6, so extra tempo plus two hot-shooting teams. The Coin toss total (model 231.3, blend 235.9, market 237.5) all missed by 32 to 39.

The market-weighted margin (model IND -1.0 vs market MIA +8.5) pulled our pick to MIA by 5.6; the model-only margin was 21 off, the blend 14.4 and the market 11.5, so the safeguard helped against the model but the market was still better. Giannis (31 min) and Adebayo (33) played a normal load, so garbage time did not matter.

verdict: Right winner, far bigger: Minnesota won 127-101 (by 26) against our 7.9 (market 6.5). Total 228 was 4.5 over the posted 223.5.

factors.text: Minnesota made 51 of 96 (62.5% effective FG) with 18 of 43 threes and 62 points in the paint; the Clippers made 12 of 30 threes but 35 of 85 overall, and committed 18 turnovers (28 points off turnovers for Minnesota).

The spread was 6.5, below the 10-point blowout flag, but the game became a blowout anyway: McDaniels (23 pts) played 33, Ball 29 and Gobert 30, while Clippers starters sat 22 to 31 minutes. Slip legs on this game would have been at risk even without the flag.
Minnesota played without Anthony Edwards and DiVincenzo, the Clippers without Ingram, Beal, Strus and Niederhauser; bench scoring was 51 to 40 for Minnesota.
Both the model (9.0) and market (6.5) were far from 26; part of it was Bones Hyland 19 off the bench in 20 minutes and Clippers shooting 2 of 11 for Wagler.

verdict: Wrong winner and our biggest miss: Golden State won 112-95 (by 17) as a 3.5-point underdog while we had the Lakers by 3.6. Total 207 was 27.5 under the posted 234.5.

factors.text: Golden State made 22 of 46 threes (Curry 8 of 14 for 31, Melton 4 of 6, Podziemski 4 of 9) and 55.1% effective FG; the Lakers made 11 of 39 threes and 33 of 82 overall.
The Lakers turned it over 22 times (Reaves 8, Doncic 3) against Golden State's 17, and Golden State had 31 assists to 18. Doncic scored 37 on 12 of 27 but the team shot 47.0% effective FG.
About 99 and 98 possessions, in line with the slate (99.6), so the 27.5-point miss on the total was efficiency (Lakers 95), not tempo.
Both the model (-3.7) and market (-3.5) margins agreed, so no safeguard applied; both were 20 points wide. Coin toss total correctly stayed ungraded (the 25/75 blend 235.1 was 28 high).

verdict: Right winner, close to expectation: Denver won 127-120 against our 4.0 (market 4.5). Total 247 was 15.5 over the posted 231.5.

factors.text: Denver made 20 of 37 threes (54%) with Murray 39 on 7 of 9 and 12 of 15 free throws, and Braun 31 on 7 of 9 threes. Phoenix made 46 of 94 and scored 50 in the paint but shot 10 of 11 from the line to Denver's 23 of 30.
About 100 and 99 possessions, so the extra 15.5 points on the total came from Denver's 65.0% effective FG, not tempo.
Jokic scored 18 on 8 of 13 with 10 assists and 5 turnovers in 37 minutes; the win came from Murray (39) and Braun (31), Phoenix's Dillon Brooks scored 22 in only 21 minutes with 4 fouls.

Murray and Braun combined for 70 points on 21 of 34 from the field and 14 of 18 from three, which is mostly hot shooting; Phoenix's 123.7 allowed average suggested the over was possible but not a lean.

headline: Winners 6 of 10: all 3 High picks won, but 3 of 5 Mediums lost and totals missed by 19 points

stats.label: Winners
stats.note: High 3 of 3 (Boston, Detroit, Minnesota); Medium 2 of 5 (Miami and Denver won; Toronto, Houston and the Lakers lost); Low 1 of 2 (Washington won as the flagged underdog, New York lost). The market favourite won only 5 of 10.

stats.label: Total leans
stats.note: All ten totals were Coin toss under the 6-game safeguard, so none were graded. Totals finished from 174 to 270 against posted lines of 218.5 to 237.5: six games were 15 or more points away (Charlotte-Washington -44.5, New York-Philadelphia -35.5, Indiana-Miami +32.5, Lakers-Warriors -27.5, Detroit-Brooklyn -18.5, Denver-Phoenix +15.5).

stats.label: Total error

right: All three High-confidence moneylines won (Boston by 14 against a 14.5 spread, Detroit by 16, Minnesota by 26), and Boston's margin was within 0.3 of our projection.
The Washington underdog flag was right: the model had them at +4.5 at home against a market of -1.5 and they won by 16.
Coin toss totals avoided total leans in games that finished 44.5 under and 32.5 over, where any lean would have lost.
Margin weighting kept us level with the market (11.2 against 11.0); on Orlando-Toronto and Indiana-Miami the market weighting cut the miss from 22.8 and 21.0 to 15.6 and 14.4.
wrong: Medium picks went 2 of 5. Toronto lost 121-114 to a short-handed Orlando that made 18 of 34 threes; Houston lost to Dallas without Sengun and Sheppard while making 7 of 29 threes; the Lakers lost by 17 as a 3.5-point favourite after 22 turnovers and Golden State made 22 of 46 threes. All three are mostly shooting variance and turnovers, but the injuries (Sengun) and thin Orlando roster are real contributors.

Totals: the blend and the market missed by about 19 either way. Charlotte shot 12 of 56 from three and Washington 29 of 35 at the line (174 total), and Indiana-Miami (270) was 104 possessions with 57.7% and 67.7% effective FG; neither the 4-5 game averages nor the lines could see those swings.

New York-Philadelphia and Charlotte-Washington show the cost of weighting the market: the model margin was closer in both (1.4 against 5.0, and 11.5 against 15.7) but the blend still picked correctly only on Washington.
Blowouts at spreads under 10 (Minnesota +26, Miami +20, Detroit +16, Washington +16) were the main source of margin error; 3 of 10 games finished 17 or more points from the spread.
change: Keep the market-weighted totals until teams have 6+ games: model-only totals missed by 20.4 against 19.2 for our blend, a tiny gap over ten games.

Keep the 30/70 margin weighting for model-market gaps over 5 points: it helped on Orlando-Toronto and Indiana-Miami and hurt on New York-Philadelphia and Charlotte-Washington, so over these four games the blend missed by 12.7, the model alone by 14.2 and the market by 12.0: close to neutral.
Consider a larger blowout flag for slips: the three biggest margins this slate (Minnesota 26, Miami 20, Golden State 17) came with spreads under 10, so a spread-only threshold missed them.
Add an injury-news timestamp to Medium picks: Sengun (Houston) was only questionable on the morning report and did not play.
caveats: Ten games, so every error figure is noisy. The feed has no second-chance points and bench points for Chicago-Boston and Denver-Phoenix; possessions are estimated (FGA + 0.44 FTA - ORB + TOV). No prop or slip picks for these games were on file, so those are not graded.

right: Five of six Medium moneylines won: Portland, Memphis, Cleveland, San Antonio and Houston all won by 10 or more, and Houston (the 68% pick with a model edge of 15 points over the price) won by 21.
The 30/70 market weighting helped where it applied: Minnesota-San Antonio finished 1.9 off our margin (model alone 9.9 off) and Cleveland-Milwaukee 17.5 off (model alone 22.1).

wrong: Atlanta (Medium, 61%) lost by 22 at New Orleans as a 3.5-point favourite: the Hawks made 8 of 46 threes and turned it over eight times in the first quarter, a shooting and turnover outlier more than a read on the matchup.

The Charlotte underdog pick (Low, 52%) lost 109-104 to Philadelphia without LeBron James and Embiid, and the Lean under on the total missed by half a point (213 against 212.5). The model total (198.5) was 14.5 off, the market 0.5 off.
